sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu maithilīṃ sītām āśramaṃ saṃpraveśitām saṃtāpam akarod ghoraṃ lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ
english: Having seen Sītā, daughter of Mithilā, led into the hermitage, Lakṣmaṇa, his heart afflicted, was seized with dreadful anguish.

sanskrit: abravīc ca mahātejāḥ sumantraṃ mantrasārathim sītāsaṃtāpajaṃ duḥkhaṃ paśya rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: And that great-spirited one spoke to Sumantra, the charioteer who was also a counsellor: "Behold the grief born of Sītā's suffering that afflicts the wise Rāma."

sanskrit: ato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu rāghavasya bhaviṣyati patnīṃ śuddhasamācārāṃ visṛjya janakātmajām
english: "What greater sorrow could befall Rāghava than this — that he has abandoned the daughter of Janaka, his wife of pure conduct?"

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ daivād ahaṃ manye rāghavasya vinābhavam vaidehyā sārathe sārdhaṃ daivaṃ hi duratikramam
english: "Clearly I think it is fate that causes Rāghava's separation from Vaidehī, O charioteer; for fate is indeed impossible to transgress."

sanskrit: yo hi devān sagandharvān asurān saha rākṣasaiḥ nihanyād rāghavaḥ kruddhaḥ sa daivam anuvartate
english: "He who, when angered, could slay gods together with gandharvas, asuras and rākṣasas — that Rāghava now follows the dictates of fate."

sanskrit: purā mama pitur vākyair daṇḍake vijane vane uṣito navavarṣāṇi pañca caiva sudāruṇe
english: "Formerly, by the command of my father, he dwelt in the dreadful desolate Daṇḍaka forest for nine years and five."

sanskrit: tato duḥkhataraṃ bhūyaḥ sītāyā vipravāsanam paurāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā nṛśaṃsaṃ pratibhāti me
english: "Yet even more grievous than that seems to me the exile of Sītā, upon hearing the cruel words of the townspeople."

sanskrit: ko nu dharmāśrayaḥ sūta karmaṇy asmin yaśohare maithilīṃ prati saṃprāptaḥ paurair hīnārthavādibhiḥ
english: "What support of righteousness, O charioteer, can be found in this honour-destroying act toward Maithilī, carried out on account of the lowly words of the townspeople?"

sanskrit: etā bahuvidhā vācaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇabhāṣitāḥ sumantraḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Having heard these many words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, Sumantra joined his palms in reverence and spoke these words:

sanskrit: na saṃtāpas tvayā kāryaḥ saumitre maithilīṃ prati dṛṣṭam etat purā vipraiḥ pitus te lakṣmaṇāgrataḥ
english: "You should not grieve, O Saumitri, concerning Maithilī; this was foreseen before by the brāhmaṇas in the presence of your father, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati dṛḍhaṃ rāmo duḥkhaprāyo 'lpasaukhyavān tvāṃ caiva maithilīṃ caiva śatrughnabharatau tathā saṃtyajiṣyati dharmātmā kālena mahatā mahān
english: "Rāma will surely be one whose lot is mostly sorrow and little happiness; the righteous great one will abandon you and Maithilī, and likewise Śatrughna and Bharata, after a great span of time."

sanskrit: na tv idaṃ tvayi vaktavyaṃ saumitre bharate 'pi vā rājñā vo 'vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ durvāsā yad uvāca ha
english: "But this should not be told to you, O Saumitri, nor to Bharata — for what Durvāsas once said was not spoken by the king as a communication to you."

sanskrit: mahārājasamīpe ca mama caiva nararṣabha ṛṣiṇā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhasya ca saṃnidhau
english: "Those words were spoken by the sage in the presence of the great king, of myself, O bull among men, and in the presence of Vasiṣṭha."

sanskrit: ṛṣes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā mām āha puruṣarṣabhaḥ sūta na kva cid evaṃ te vaktavyaṃ janasaṃnidhau
english: "Having heard the sage's words, that bull among men said to me: 'O charioteer, this must never be told by you in any gathering of people.'"

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ lokapālasya vākyaṃ tat susamāhitaḥ naiva jātv anṛtaṃ kuryām iti me saumya darśanam
english: "I, with concentrated mind, accepted those words of that guardian of the world; I would never act falsely toward them — such is my conviction, O gentle one."

sanskrit: sarvathā nāsty avaktavyaṃ mayā saumya tavāgrataḥ yadi te śravaṇe śraddhā śrūyatāṃ raghunandana
english: "There is nothing at all that I ought not speak before you, O gentle one; if you have faith in hearing it, let it be heard, O delight of the Raghu line."

sanskrit: yady apy ahaṃ narendreṇa rahasyaṃ śrāvitaḥ purā tac cāpy udāhariṣyāmi daivaṃ hi duratikramam
english: "Even though I was formerly made to hear this secret by the king of men, I shall nonetheless recount it — for fate is impossible to transgress."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya gambhīrārthapadaṃ mahat tathyaṃ brūhīti saumitriḥ sūtaṃ vākyam athābravīt
english: Having heard his speech, profound in meaning and weighty, Saumitri then spoke these words to the charioteer: "Speak the truth."

sanskrit: tathā saṃcoditaḥ sūto lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā tad vākyam ṛṣiṇā proktaṃ vyāhartum upacakrame
english: Thus urged by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, the charioteer began to relate the words that had been spoken by the sage.

sanskrit: purā nāmnā hi durvāsā atreḥ putro mahāmuniḥ vasiṣṭhasyāśrame puṇye sa vārṣikyam uvāsa ha
english: "Long ago, the great sage Durvāsas, son of Atri, dwelt through the rainy season in the holy hermitage of Vasiṣṭha."

sanskrit: tam āśramaṃ mahātejāḥ pitā te sumahāyaśāḥ purodhasaṃ mahātmānaṃ didṛkṣur agamat svayam
english: "Your father, of great splendour and most exalted fame, went there himself, wishing to see that great-souled priest."

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā sūryasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā upaviṣṭaṃ vasiṣṭhasya savye pārśve mahāmunim tau munī tāpasaśreṣṭhau vinītas tv abhyavādayat
english: "Seeing the great sage seated at the left side of Vasiṣṭha, blazing with energy like the sun, he reverently saluted those two sages, foremost among ascetics."

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ pūjito rājā svāgatenāsanena ca pādyena phalamūlaiś ca so 'py āste munibhiḥ saha
english: "The king, honoured by them with a welcome, a seat, water for the feet, and fruits and roots, sat there with the sages."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tatropaviṣṭānāṃ tās tāḥ sumadhurāḥ kathāḥ babhūvuḥ paramarṣīṇāṃ madhyādityagate 'hani
english: "As they sat there, those most noble sages exchanged many sweet conversations while the sun passed its midday course."

sanskrit: tataḥ kathāyāṃ kasyāṃ cit prāñjaliḥ pragraho nṛpaḥ uvāca taṃ mahātmānam atreḥ putraṃ tapodhanam
english: "Then, in the midst of a certain conversation, the king, with joined palms and restrained manner, addressed that great-souled son of Atri, rich in austerity."

sanskrit: bhagavan kiṃpramāṇena mama vaṃśo bhaviṣyati kimāyuś ca hi me rāmaḥ putrāś cānye kimāyuṣaḥ
english: "'Revered one, how extensive will my lineage be? What will be the lifespan of my Rāma, and what the lifespans of my other sons?'"

sanskrit: rāmasya ca sutā ye syus teṣām āyuḥ kiyad bhavet kāmyayā bhagavan brūhi vaṃśasyāsya gatiṃ mama
english: "'What lifespan will the sons of Rāma have? Out of devotion, revered one, tell me the course of this my lineage.'"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rājño daśarathasya tu durvāsāḥ sumahātejā vyāhartum upacakrame
english: "Hearing the words spoken by King Daśaratha, Durvāsas of immense energy began to speak."

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāḥ patī rāmo dīrghakālaṃ bhaviṣyati sukhinaś ca samṛddhāś ca bhaviṣyanty asya cānujāḥ
english: "'Rāma will be lord of Ayodhyā for a long time; his younger brothers too will be prosperous and happy.'"

sanskrit: kasmiṃś cit karaṇe tvāṃ ca maithilīṃ ca yaśasvinīm saṃtyajiṣyati dharmātmā kālena mahatā kila
english: "'For a certain reason the righteous one will abandon you and the glorious Maithilī after a great span of time.'"

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasraṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca rāmo rājyam upāsitvā brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyati
english: "'Having attended to his kingship for ten thousand years and ten hundred years, Rāma will depart to the world of Brahmā.'"

sanskrit: samṛddhair hayamedhaiś ca iṣṭvā parapuraṃjayaḥ rājavaṃśāṃś ca kākutstho bahūn saṃsthāpayiṣyati
english: "'Having worshipped with prosperous aśvamedha sacrifices, the conqueror of enemy cities, the scion of Kākutstha, will establish many royal lineages.'"

sanskrit: sa sarvam akhilaṃ rājño vaṃśasyāsya gatāgatam ākhyāya sumahātejās tūṣṇīm āsīn mahādyutiḥ
english: "Having narrated in full all the comings and goings of this royal lineage, that sage of immense energy and great brilliance fell silent."

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃbhūte munau tasmin rājā daśarathas tadā abhivādya mahātmānau punar āyāt purottamam
english: "When the sage had fallen silent, King Daśaratha then saluted those two great souls and returned to the finest of cities."

sanskrit: etad vaco mayā tatra muninā vyāhṛtaṃ purā śrutaṃ hṛdi ca nikṣiptaṃ nānyathā tad bhaviṣyati
english: "These words spoken by the sage there long ago were heard by me and laid up in my heart; it shall not be otherwise than this."

sanskrit: evaṃ gate na saṃtāpaṃ gantum arhasi rāghava sītārthe rāghavārthe vā dṛḍho bhava narottama
english: "Things being so, you ought not fall into grief, O Rāghava — whether for Sītā's sake or for Rāghava's sake; be resolute, O best of men."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ sūtasya paramādbhutam praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt
english: Hearing the most wonderful words spoken by the charioteer, he was seized with incomparable joy and said: "Well spoken, well spoken!"

sanskrit: tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ sūtalakṣmaṇayoḥ pathi astam arko gato vāsaṃ gomatyāṃ tāv athoṣatuḥ
english: As the charioteer and Lakṣmaṇa conversed thus along the road, the sun went to its setting; and those two then spent the night at the Gomatī river.

sanskrit: tatra tāṃ rajanīm uṣya gomatyāṃ raghunandanaḥ prabhāte punar utthāya lakṣmaṇaḥ prayayau tadā
english: Having passed that night there at the Gomatī, the delight of the Raghu line, Lakṣmaṇa, rose again at dawn and then set forth.

sanskrit: tato 'rdhadivase prāpte praviveśa mahārathaḥ ayodhyāṃ ratnasaṃpūrṇāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām
english: Then, when midday arrived, that great warrior entered Ayodhyā, filled with jewels and thronged with joyful and prosperous people.

sanskrit: saumitris tu paraṃ dainyaṃ jagāma sumahāmatiḥ rāmapādau samāsādya vakṣyāmi kim ahaṃ gataḥ
english: But Saumitri, that most great-minded one, was overcome with the deepest wretchedness: "What shall I say when I stand before the feet of Rāma — 'I have gone and done it'?"

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ cintayānasya bhavanaṃ śaśisaṃnibham rāmasya paramodāraṃ purastāt samadṛśyata
english: As he brooded thus, before him appeared the most magnificent palace of Rāma, resembling the moon.

sanskrit: rājñas tu bhavanadvāri so 'vatīrya narottamaḥ avāṅmukho dīnamanāḥ prāviveśānivāritaḥ
english: That best of men descended at the gate of the king's palace, and entered with downcast face and grieving heart, unhindered.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṃ dīnam āsīnaṃ paramāsane netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyāṃ dadarśāgrajam agrataḥ
english: He saw Rāghava, sorrowful and seated upon the high seat; with eyes full of tears he beheld his elder brother before him.

sanskrit: jagrāha caraṇau tasya lakṣmaṇo dīnacetanaḥ uvāca dīnayā vācā prāñjaliḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa, his heart afflicted, clasped his feet, and spoke with a despondent voice, with joined palms, composed in manner:

sanskrit: āryasyājñāṃ puraskṛtya visṛjya janakātmajām gaṅgātīre yathoddiṣṭe vālmīker āśrame śubhe punar asmy āgato vīra pādamūlam upāsitum
english: "Having placed foremost the command of the noble one, and having abandoned the daughter of Janaka at the auspicious hermitage of Vālmīki on the bank of the Gaṅgā as directed, I have come again, O hero, to attend at your feet."

sanskrit: mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra kālasya gatir īdṛśī tvadvidhā na hi śocanti sattvavanto manasvinaḥ
english: "Do not grieve, O tiger among men; such is the way of time. Men of your kind — those possessed of courage and wisdom — do not grieve.

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam
english: "All accumulations end in diminishment; all that rises ends in falling; all unions end in separation; and life ends in death."

sanskrit: śaktas tvam ātmanātmānaṃ vijetuṃ manasaiva hi lokān sarvāṃś ca kākutstha kiṃ punar duḥkham īdṛśam
english: "You are capable of conquering yourself — and indeed all worlds — by the mind alone, O scion of Kākutstha; how much more then a sorrow such as this?"

sanskrit: nedṛśeṣu vimuhyanti tvadvidhāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ yadarthaṃ maithilī tyaktā apavādabhayān nṛpa
english: "Bulls among men of your kind are not bewildered by such things as that for which Maithilī was abandoned — out of fear of censure, O king."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla dhairyeṇa susamāhitaḥ tyajemāṃ durbalāṃ buddhiṃ saṃtāpaṃ mā kuruṣva ha
english: "Therefore you, O tiger among men, steadfast in fortitude, abandon this weakness of mind; do not allow yourself to be consumed by anguish."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kākutstho lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā uvāca parayā prītyā saumitriṃ mitravatsalam
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, the scion of Kākutstha spoke with the highest affection to Saumitri, who was devoted as a friend:

sanskrit: evam etan naraśreṣṭha yathā vadasi lakṣmaṇa paritoṣaś ca me vīra mama kāryānuśāsane
english: "It is exactly as you say, O best of men, O Lakṣmaṇa; and I am satisfied, O hero, by your guidance in my duty."

sanskrit: nirvṛtiś ca kṛtā saumya saṃtāpaś ca nirākṛtaḥ bhavadvākyaiḥ sumadhurair anunīto 'smi lakṣmaṇa
english: "Contentment has been made, O gentle one, and anguish has been dispelled; by your very sweet words I have been consoled, O Lakṣmaṇa."
